title: Allergic reaction
reference: NASA ISS Medical Operations: Anaphylaxis and Hypersensitivity Protocol (NASA-STD-3001).

q1.text: Are there critical anaphylactic signs: stridor, throat tightness, severe wheezing, difficulty swallowing, or sudden dizziness/collapse?

i_epi.text: INJECT EPINEPHRINE IMMEDIATELY: Administer Epinephrine Auto-Injector (EpiPen 0.3 mg) into anterolateral mid-thigh. Apply high-flow O2 mask and place patient horizontal with legs elevated.

t_epi.text: Monitor vitals, airway patency, and blood pressure continuously for 5 minutes post-epinephrine injection.

q_epi_resp.text: Are respiratory distress and hemodynamics improving after 5 minutes?

i_epi_stable.text: Administer secondary medications: Diphenhydramine (Benadryl) 50 mg IV/oral and Methylprednisolone (Solu-Medrol) 125 mg IV. Keep under continuous observation.

i_epi_repeat.text: REFRACTORY ANAPHYLAXIS: Administer second dose of Epinephrine 0.3 mg into opposite thigh. Initiate IV normal saline bolus (1000 mL) to combat vasodilation.

q2.text: Is there widespread urticaria (hives), facial puffiness, or intense generalized pruritus without airway compromise?

i_moderate.text: MODERATE ALLERGIC REACTION: Administer oral Diphenhydramine 50 mg and Cetirizine 10 mg. Monitor airway and vital signs every 15 minutes.

q3.text: Are vital signs (SpO2, blood pressure, heart rate) completely stable and is swelling contained to the skin?

i_mild.text: MILD / LOCALIZED DERMAL REACTION: Apply Hydrocortisone 1% cream to affected skin. Administer oral Cetirizine 10 mg.

i_escalate_allergy.text: Signs of systemic progression. Prepare Epinephrine auto-injector at bedside; notify Medical Officer.

end_monitor.text: Allergic reaction contained. Monitor for biphasic reaction over next 12 hours; isolate suspected allergen from food or cabin supplies.

end_escalate.text: ANAPHYLAXIS ESCALATION: Flight Surgeon alert active. Emergency airway kit at bedside; monitor for rebound collapse.
